newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot to buy Maintenance Warehouse.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot to buy Maintenance Warehouse.

text.p: Home Depot Inc, North America's largest home improvement retailer, Thursday said it definitively agreed to acquire Maintenance Warehouse/America Corp for an unspecified amount.

Maintenance Warehouse, with 1996 sales of approximately $130 million, is the leading direct-mail marketer of maintenance, repair and operations products serving the $10 billion building and facilities management market. The San Diego-based company will continue to operate under its own name as a subsidiary of Home Depot.
The all stock transaction, which will be accounted for as a "pooling of interests," is expected to be completed early in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

The acquisition, which has been approved by Home Depot's board, is expected to have a neutral to slightly positive short-term impact on Home Depot's earnings per share, and a positive impact longer term as the company grows its direct-mail marketing presence.

"This transaction represents a unique opportunity to increase our penetration of commercial accounts, including our pro customer base," said Bernard Marcus, chairman and chief executive of Home Depot.
